episodes.title: How AMD's Lisa Su Views the Future of AI
episodes.description:
How AMD's Lisa Su Is Thinking About AI

13 Dec 2024

---

In a conversation with HBR editor-in-chief Adi Ignatius, Lisa Su, CEO of leading semiconductor company AMD, discusses its evolution toward high-performance and adaptive computing, the future of AI use in sectors from healthcare to tech to personal productivity, and the importance of responsible risk-taking. She advocates for fast experimentation and implementation while ensuring safety through initiatives like AMD’s Responsible AI Council, active learning within the organization and among industry peers and partners, and the hiring of diverse talent to drive innovation. 

Time Magazine recently named Su their "CEO of the Year."

episodes.title: Silicon Drama Episode 13: Altman’s Agent Finds the Internet, Amodei’s Claude Breaks an 87-Year Conjecture, Lisa Su Ships Helios
episodes.description:
An OpenAI agent found the internet, escaped its intended controls and breached Hugging Face. Claude helped produce a 216-character counterexample to an 87-year-old mathematical conjecture. And Lisa Su rolled AMD’s Helios challenge to NVIDIA onto the loading dock.

In this Deep Dive Podcast:
• Jensen Huang expands NVIDIA’s industrial kingdom• Sundar Pichai wins the cloud while Europe opens Google’s search-data vault• Satya Nadella sells Europe another version of digital sovereignty• AI data centers collide with power grids, water supplies and public resistance• Elon Musk delivers more Teslas while margins and robotaxi promises fall behind• FLUX moves from visual generation onto Audi’s factory floor

Plus: Suno’s massive data breach, the flood of AI-generated music, Intel’s recovery, brain-computer interfaces, microreactors for AI infrastructure and the latest Silicon Drama Power Board.

Which matters more for AI’s future: The agent that escaped its controls or the model that helped crack an 87-year-old problem?

Silicon Drama: Technology news, told as a power drama.

episodes.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su Live on TBPN | Oliver Cameron, Mohammad Norouzi, Anjney Midha, Lisa Su
episodes.description:
(03:31) - Oliver Cameron, co-founder and CEO of Odyssey, discusses the development of foundational world models—AI systems capable of understanding physics, causality, and human behavior—to enhance various industries, including robotics, gaming, and autonomous vehicles. He highlights the limitations of current AI systems, which are often narrowly trained, and advocates for more generalized models that can be fine-tuned for specific tasks. Cameron also emphasizes the importance of diverse data sources in training these models to ensure robustness and adaptability across different applications.

(21:09) - Mohammad Norouzi, CEO and co-founder of Ideogram, discusses the company's mission to enhance creativity through generative AI, focusing on design and marketing applications. He highlights the challenges of achieving consistency in AI-generated images, particularly for brand marketing and product design, and emphasizes the importance of data sovereignty for enterprises, noting that Ideogram's compact, open-weight models can be hosted on-premises to address these concerns. Norouzi also mentions Ideogram's collaboration with AMD to optimize their models for AMD's hardware, tailoring model architectures to balance price, performance, and latency.

(31:42) - Anjney Midha is the founder of AMP PBC, an AI infrastructure startup, and a former general partner at Andreessen Horowitz. In the transcript, he discusses the importance of "output maxing" in AI development, emphasizing the need for efficient utilization of computational resources to maintain a competitive edge. He highlights that only 15% of data center capacity in the U.S. is utilized, calling this underutilization a national security concern, and advocates for smarter, more efficient use of existing infrastructure to stay at the forefront of AI advancements.

(55:12) - 𝕏 Timeline Reactions

(01:27:52) - Lisa Su, born in Taiwan and raised in the U.S., is the chair and CEO of AMD, renowned for revitalizing the company since 2014. In the conversation, she highlights the rapid evolution of AI, emphasizing the need for AMD to accelerate its technology roadmaps to meet market demands. Su also underscores AMD's commitment to building great products through collaboration and open ecosystems, reflecting the company's culture of partnership and innovation.

episodes.title: Possible: Lisa Su on semiconductors, compute, and big bets
episodes.description:
What’s the role of semiconductors—and the companies that make them—in powering human progress? What does it look like to innovate thoughtfully in a landscape where the demand for power may be higher than the supply? With AI evolving faster and faster, how can we keep up?
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) CEO Lisa Su joins the show to talk about hardware, global manufacturing, and risk-taking. She shares what she has learned leading AMD from near-bankruptcy a decade ago to its current standing as one of the world’s leading chipmakers. Lisa also weighs in on geopolitics, the AI arms race, startups, what makes her want to hire someone, and AI’s enormous potential to advance healthcare for humankind.

episodes.title: KI-Chancen noch unterschätzt | AMD CEO Lisa Su.
episodes.podcast_title: Wall Street mit Markus Koch - featured by Handelsblatt
episodes.description:
Die Wall Street ist sich darüber einig, dass wir uns bei den KI-Werten in einer Spekulationsblase befinden, mit Vergleichen zur Dotcom-Bubble der 1990er Jahre. Die Frage ist allerdings, in welcher Zeitspanne wir uns genau befinden. Befinden wir uns erst in der Phase des Jahres 1995, stehen wir erst am Anfang des Booms. Der Hedgefondsmanager Paul Tudor geht davon aus, dass die aktuelle Phase eher mit dem Jahr 1998 zu vergleichen ist, mit dem finalen und starken letzten Melt-up noch vor uns. Vor dem Opening hebt Dell Technologies die Ertrags- und Umsatzaussichten an. IBM profitiert von einer neuen Kooperation mit Anthropic, und tendiert freundlich. Bei AMD sehen wir wiederum weiter steigende Kursziele. Wells Fargo sieht die Aktie bis auf $275 steigen. Die UBS hat ein Ziel von $265. Die Ertrags- und Umsatzaussichten werden teils deutlich angehoben. Auch der CEO von AMD betont, dass viele das Potenzial von KI noch unterschätzen.

episodes.title: View From The Top: “Lisa Su Is Still Curious About How Things Work”
episodes.description:
This week on If/Then, we’re sharing an episode of View From The Top: The Podcast, an audio series featuring leaders from around the world in conversation with MBA students. Recorded live at the CEMEX Auditorium at Stanford Graduate School of Business, episodes feature insights on effective leadership, the values that guide it, and lessons learned along the way.
Lisa Su, the chair and CEO of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), leads one of the world’s most influential technology companies, a pioneer in high-performance computing and designer of chips that power everything from cellphones to supercomputers.
Su joins Michael Liu, MBA ’25, to talk about what it takes to stay on the cutting edge of technology, the tremendous potential of artificial intelligence, and why her superpower may be her commitment to learning.
“Careers are very much by chance,” Su says. “The nice thing about my early career is I was lucky enough to have bosses who asked me all the time, ‘What do you want to be when you grow up?’ And I was like, ‘I don't know. Let me think about [it]...what I like to believe is the ability to learn at each step was what really helped me in my career.”
This conversation was recorded on February 24, 2025. 
More Resources:
    •  Lisa Su
    •  GSB Insights 
    •  View From The Top

episodes.title: Episode #2: Lisa Su, AMD, Nina Kuscsik and the Glass Cliff
episodes.podcast_title: Hypatia: Women Who Win - with Patricia Lizarraga
episodes.description:
In this week’s podcast episode, we spotlight two trailblazers who turned impossible odds into historic wins. 
·    Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, who took the reins when the company was on the brink - and led a $200 billion turnaround. 
·    Nina Kuscsik, the first woman to officially win the NYC Marathon, who changed sports history just by showing up. 
We unpack the “glass cliff” phenomenon - the reality that women are often handed leadership only when failure seems likely - and how these women didn’t just survive the cliff edge. They soared. 
Plus, we revisit the moment in 2018 when F1 broadcaster Martin Brundle approached Lisa Su on the grid and asked, “Do you speak English?” - a striking reminder that even the most powerful women are still underestimated. 
 This episode is about resilience, perception, and what it really means to lead when no one expects you to succeed.
